..
Issued at 300 AM EDT Fri Oct 2 2026

Currently-Today... KMLB radar imagery shows isolated showers over 
the Treasure Coast, Okeechobee county, and Osceola county. 
GOES-19 satellite imagery and local observations indicate partly 
to mostly cloudy skies across east central Florida. Temperatures 
are currently in the low 70s to low 80s with dew points in the 
upper 60s to mid 70s. Analysis charts show onshore low level flow 
in place. Additionally, the Bermuda high (~1023mb) extends across 
the western Atlantic with an inverted trough near the Bahamas. 

Isolated to scattered showers and lightning storms are forecast this 
morning mainly from Cape Canaveral southwards before rain chances
increase from the southeast to northwest across east central 
Florida into the afternoon. The greatest chance for scattered to 
numerous showers and lightning storms is between 12PM and 8PM 
today. Guidance indicates MLCAPE up to 1,000-3,200 J/kg, 0-6km 
shear up to 5-15kts, PWATs between 2.0-2.4", and 500mb
temperatures at -6C to -5C. Thus, the potential exists for 
isolated strong storms capable of occasional to frequent 
lightning, wind gusts up to 35-45mph, and heavy rainfall (up to 
2-4" in 60 minutes); the greatest potential for heavy rainfall, as
well as minor flooding of low lying areas and roadways will be 
from Cape Canaveral southwards today. Afternoon highs in the upper
80s to low 90s and heat index values up to 98F to 106F degrees 
are forecast. There is a Moderate HeatRisk which can affect anyone
who is sensitive to heat without adequate cooling and hydration. 

The Weekend... A mostly persistent forecast is expected through the 
weekend with onshore flow in place and as high pressure to the north-
northeast gradually shifts east over the western Atlantic. 
Meanwhile, low pressure is forecast to move east over North 
Carolina on Sunday with a cold front that will extend across the 
Deep South. However, the aforementioned inverted trough is 
expected to "wash out" over the Bahamas; this will limit the 
potential coverage of showers and lightning storms compared to the
past couple of days when coupled with a weak west coast sea 
breeze which will likely result in the highest rain chances across
the western interior of east central Florida, as well as west 
Florida. Additionally, CAMs have trended towards lower rain 
chances for Saturday and PoPs have the potential to be reduced 
further through the weekend with future model runs. Scattered to 
numerous showers and lightning storms are forecast to develop 
Saturday afternoon and evening with the greatest chances between 
2PM-7PM. Expect a similar forecast on Sunday. The potential exists
for isolated strong storms capable of occasional to frequent 
lightning, wind gusts up to 35-45mph, and heavy rainfall (up to 
1-2"+ in 60 minutes). Afternoon highs in the upper 80s to low 90s 
with heat index values up to 98F-106F degrees are forecast. Above 
normal (~4F-6F+) to near record lows in the mid to upper 70s are 
forecast. There is a Moderate HeatRisk with small pockets of Major
HeatRisk across the Treasure Coast. 

Monday-Thursday... Deterministic models and the LREF-clusters are
in good agreement that the ridge over the eastern CONUS will 
break down and weaken into Sunday before a longwave trough deepens
over the eastern CONUS, as well as the Deep South on 
Monday/Tuesday. At the surface, a cold front/stationary boundary 
is forecast to meander across east central Florida late Monday 
into Tuesday before stalling over east central Florida - or just 
to the north - through midweek. Therefore, rain chances remain 
high each day with likely rain chances (70-90%) through Thursday. 
Deterministic models show 500mb temperatures at around -5C to -4C 
which is likely to limit the stronger storm potential when coupled
with cloud cover and only moderate MUCAPE values. However, heavy 
rainfall and flooding of low lying areas, as well as roadways will
be a concern each day with slow storm motions and likely training
showers/storms forecast. The week will start off with seasonable 
high temperatures and above normal low temperatures before 
decreasing behind the front (mainly over and to the north of 
Melbourne) Tuesday and into midweek. Temperatures will be 
dependent on the position of the front each day, therefore, there 
is greater uncertainty than usual in that regard.
